we design linear precoders and equalizers for multiuser FBMC-OQAm under strong channel frequency selectivitiy.
the proposed single-tap precoders/decoders for FBMC-OQAmultiuser MIMO systems under a strong channel frequency-selectivity can be designed using the proposed design criterion.

In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel approach for linear precoder and decoder design for FBMC in the presence of a strong channel selectivity.
the design of linear precoder and decoders for multi-user MIMO filter bank multicarrier (MIMO-FBMC).
the design of single-tap precoders and deciders for a multiuser MIMO FBMA system under strong channel frequency selectivities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the design of single-tap precoders or decodes for FBMC is possible in the case of channel frequency selectivity, provided that the number of BS antenna is larger than the total number of users.

the proposed design is a low complexity solution that is able to compensate for the effect of the channel frequency selectiveness in the downlink as long as the number BS antennas is larger that the number of users.

, in the case of FBMC-OQAMS, the proposed single tap per-subcarriers linear precoders and/or decoders are able to achieve the performance of a classical linear precoders and/decoders in the case of flat channel frequency selectivty.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed precoders and decodes are optimal for strong channel selectivity, and they can be used in the case of weak channel selectivity.
the design of precoders/decoders for multiuser filterbank multicarriers under strong channel frequency selectivities has been addressed for the first time.
we propose a low complexity solution that can be implemented in the frequency domain and is robust against channel frequency selectivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the case of FBMC, the channel frequency selectiveness can be compensated by the BS even if it does not have perfect knowledge of the channel state.
the proposed design can provide a significant performance improvement over the classical approaches that assume a flat channel frequency selectiviy.
a single tap per subcarrier is sufficient to compensate for the distortion due to channel frequency selectivity in a FBMC context.
